purpose: Model a privately originated, collectively governed monetary system that may evolve from a payment asset into a supranational monetary regime while testing distributional, stability and transition effects.

K_M.name: K-Money
K_M.design_objective: Stable purchasing power and high settlement reliability rather than speculative appreciation.
K_M.supply_governance: monetary-policy contract + external Smart Vote authority interface

K_C.name: K-Capital
K_C.design_objective: Allow broad participation in system surplus/appreciation without forcing the transaction currency itself to be a speculative asset.

multiplex_layers.semantics: authorization, settlement, receipts and merchant acceptance
K-denominated claims, maturity, collateral and liquidity transformation
K-Capital ownership, beneficial exposure, social dividend and concentration
optional sovereign acceptance for taxes, procurement or debt issuance; never assumed
policy proposals, expertise/integrity weighting, ratification, audit and emergency authority
real resources and supply constraints that bound non-inflationary purchasing power
observations, assumptions, hypotheses, evidence, decisions and model outputs

invariants: Payment settlement must conserve K_M across ordinary transfers: debit equals credit net of explicitly declared fees or issuance/redemption operations.
A payment credential or QR identifier is not itself canonical money and must not contain a reusable spending secret by default.
K_M monetary policy cannot be unilaterally changed by the founder.
Smart Vote outputs do not become empirical facts; policy decisions and observed outcomes remain distinct epistemic regimes.
Distributional objectives are evaluated in real resources and real wealth, not only nominal K balances.
No state transition to sovereign/fiscal acceptance is implied without an external sovereign decision.
Simulation output never has authority over the world.
